newsitem.title: UK: Pharmacia & Upjohn Aids drug wins approval.
newsitem.headline: Pharmacia & Upjohn Aids drug wins approval.

text.p: Swedish-U.S. drugs group Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said on Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Aministration (FDA) had given marketing approval to Rescriptor, a new drug for treating HIV-1 infection.
The company said in a statement that Rescriptor had been approved for use in combination with other anti-HIV drugs under the FDA's accelerated approval regulations.
Rescriptor, or delavirdine, is a member of a new class of anti-HIV drugs knowns as non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NNRTIs).
They affect the virus at different stage in its cycle from the existing drugs -- the nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors such as Glaxo-Wellcome's AZT (Retrovir), and the protease inhibitors.

NNRTIs have been enthusiastically greeted by AIDS researchers, who say they show remarkable effects in combination therapy with RTIs. However, they can show a toxic interaction when used with protease inhibitors, which worried scientists.
Rescriptor was tested in combination with several nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors including AZT, Pharmacia said in a statement.

"Patients treated with a combination of Rescriptor plus AZT showed a significantly greater reduction in the amount of virus in the blood for one year when compared with patients treated with AZT alone," the statement said.

This "viral load" is used as one indicator of how well a drug works. But use of the drug did not affect survival or the appearance of AIDS-defining illnesses sich as Kaposi's sarcome, a common cancer among victims.

"In a completed trial comparing the combination of Rescriptor plus didanosine (ddI - Bristol-Myers Squibb's Videx)) versus ddI monotherapy, clinical benefit was not demonstrated for Rescriptor based on survival or incidence of AIDS-defining clinical events," Pharmacia said.

There was also an interaction with Merck's Crixivan (indinavir), a protease inhibitor. "When used in combination, Rescriptor increased the blood level of indinavir," Pharmacia said. Therefore, indinavir should be decreased if the two drugs were used together.

"We are prepared to distribute Rescriptor within three to four weeks in order to make it available to those patients and physicians who want to include it in combination therapy to treat HIV infection," said Goran Ando, exectuive vice president for Pharmacia.
It will sell wholesale at $6.16 per day or $2,250 a year.
